references.text: The context that establishes the principle that the Lord will choose a specific place for worship
Reiterates the requirement to eat before the Lord at the place he chooses
The Passover offering must be brought to the place the Lord chooses to let his name dwell there
The Passover offering must be slaughtered at the place your God, the Lord, chooses
The Feast of Weeks must be celebrated at the place the Lord chooses
Three times a year all men must appear before the Lord at the place he chooses
Solomon refers to the temple as the place the Lord has chosen for his name
The Lord has chosen Jerusalem so that his name may dwell there
The Lord has chosen the temple as a house for offerings
The Lord chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved
Jesus explains that worship is no longer bound to a specific place, but to spirit and truth
